findings.problem: The two theorems have the same long proof. Only the cutoff η differs (caccioppoliCutoff vs caccioppoliHeatCutoff), along with the matching three cutoff lemmas and the constant A. Both do the following in the same order. (1) Get hhtime and apply caccioppoli_I1_heat_operator. (2) Take Γ ≤ 8000000 r²/ρ³ and Γ ≥ 0. (3) Prove 0 ≤ cutoffGradientConstant/ρ. (4) Prove hcross, the termwise product bound. (5) Prove hsumabs by Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs plus abs_mul. (6) Prove hht'. (7) Run the same ~60-line calc: abs_add_le, abs_mul, mul_le_mul with hηop and hΓ, Finset.sum_le_sum, then simp with Finset.sum_const and ring. About 170 lines are duplicated, and a change to the arithmetic, such as the constants 8000000 or 5000000, must be made twice. The unused hS binding in both proofs also shows they were copied from each other.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma generic in η, with no mention of a specific cutoff:

theorem caccioppoli_I1_heat_operator_annulus_bound {η : Vec3 × ℝ → ℝ} {x₀ t₀ ρ r A : ℝ} {z : ParabolicPoint} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hr : 0 < r) (hscale : r ≤ ρ/2) (hη : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) η) (hhtime : z.2 - t₀ < r^2) (hp : (z.1 - x₀, z.2 - t₀) ∈ parabolicCylinder 0 0 ρ \ parabolicCylinder 0 0 (ρ/2)) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hηop : |timePartial η z + ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial η i i z| ≤ A) (hgrad : ∀ i, |spatialPartial η i z| ≤ cutoffGradientConstant/ρ) : |timePartial (backwardHeatCutoff η x₀ t₀ r ·) z + ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial (backwardHeatCutoff η x₀ t₀ r ·) i i z| ≤ A * (8000000*r^2/ρ^3) + 6*(cutoffGradientConstant/ρ)*(5000000*r^2/ρ^4).

Proof: this is the existing body. Obtain hCρ as (abs_nonneg _).trans (hgrad 0), which removes the by_contra block. Rewrite with caccioppoli_I1_heat_operator. Bound the first term by mul_le_mul using hηop, caccioppoli_heat_function_upper_on_annulus and backwardHeatTestFunction_nonneg. Bound the sum by abs_sum_le_sum_abs, the per-term bound mul_le_mul (hgrad i) (caccioppoli_heat_spatial_derivative_abs_on_annulus ..), and sum_const.

The cutoff version then reduces to:
exact caccioppoli_I1_heat_operator_annulus_bound hρ hr hscale (caccioppoli_cutoff_smooth ..) hhtime hp (by positivity-style proof of hden) (caccioppoli_cutoff_time_plus_laplacian_bound ..) (caccioppoli_cutoff_spatial_partial_bound x₀ t₀ ρ R hρ hR z).
The heat-cutoff version is the same with caccioppoli_heat_cutoff_smooth, caccioppoli_heat_cutoff_time_plus_laplacian_bound_on_left and caccioppoli_heat_cutoff_spatial_partial_bound, and A = 32/ρ^2 + 3*(cutoffSecondDerivativeConstant/ρ^2). Each caller keeps only its hhtime and hA proofs.
findings.benefit: This removes about 300 duplicated lines in favour of one ~70-line lemma and two short callers. The calculation lives in one place, so the 8000000/5000000 constants and the argument structure cannot drift apart. A reader sees that the only difference between the cutoffs is the bound on η. The generic lemma also drops the unused hS and the redundant nonnegativity argument.

findings.problem: The same nonnegativity proof for the constant cutoffGradientConstant is repeated verbatim in three theorems (lines 297–306, 480–489, 670–679). Each copy argues by contradiction: if the constant were negative, then C/ρ < 0, and the gradient bound at the point 0 would force a norm to be negative. The fact does not depend on the theorem it appears in, but it is re-derived each time, with an unfolding of vecEuclideanNorm and a positivity call.
findings.proposed_change: State it once, e.g. theorem cutoffGradientConstant_nonneg : 0 ≤ cutoffGradientConstant, in Cutoff.lean next to caccioppoli_spatial_cutoff_gradient_bound. Choose any x₀ and ρ = 1. By contradiction, caccioppoli_spatial_cutoff_gradient_bound x₀ 1 one_pos 0 gives 0 ≤ norm ≤ C/1. The first finding's lemma avoids it altogether by deriving 0 ≤ C/ρ from (abs_nonneg _).trans (hgrad 0). In the third theorem, replace the 10-line block with `have hCρ := div_nonneg cutoffGradientConstant_nonneg hρ.le`. The statement has no hypotheses, so it applies under every hypothesis set where the original three blocks appear.
findings.benefit: This removes three copies of a 10-line contradiction argument and names a reusable fact about the constant. It also keeps the three theorems focused on the heat-operator estimate rather than on a side property of a constant.
